planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: 1 planet at 3.037 days.

Why:
- The 3.037 d peak is overwhelmingly dominant (power 0.917, FAP ~ 0) and is not mirrored by a strong spectral-window feature there.

- The next peak at 1.608 d is much weaker and sits close enough to the half-period family of the main signal that I would not promote it to a second planet yet without seeing residuals after fitting the 3.037 d signal.
- With only an 8.2 d baseline, I also do not want to chase longer poorly constrained alternatives; 3.037 d is well within the baseline and should be fit cleanly.

Please fit the simplest model first:
- Planet b: P ≈ 3.037 days

After that, check residuals explicitly; if the engineer finds the model incomplete, I want the residual periodogram before adding any second planet.
